Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the centre. No Nishan Madushka today as he injured his left shoulder while stopping the ball in the previous game. Nuwanidu Fernando will open the innings alongside Pathum Nissanka. Richard Ngarava will start the attack for Zimbabwe. Ngarava to Nissanka. Two slips in place. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

For Sri Lanka, despite not fielding a frontline fifth bowler and instead making up the overs with a couple of individuals, they did a decent job. Dushmantha Chameera was the pick of the bowlers, finishing with figures of 3 for 52 from his 10 overs. The surface began on the slower side but quickened up as the innings progressed. However, as Ben Curran admitted, it played two-paced once the ball got softer and older. It remains to be seen how it behaves in the second innings. Zimbabwe will bank on their new-ball attack to put the tourists on the back foot early. Back in a bit for the Sri Lankan reply.

Ben Curran is up for a quick chat. He believes that they have put up a good score, and also points out that this pitch looked a bit different the usual Harare wicket. He feels great to continue his good form with the bat and contribute in this game as well. Trusts his bowler to take the learnings from the previous game and defend this total.

The tourists eventually regained some control in the middle overs, helped in part by Brendan Taylor’s struggles at the crease. Taylor fell while attempting to break free, and Curran was joined by Sean Williams. The pair took the innings forward, and with the score at 150 at the end of 31 overs, an acceleration seemed just around the corner. However, Asitha Fernando struck a decisive blow, removing both set batters in the same over. That meant the hosts were forced into a rebuild at a stage when they would have ideally looked to accelerate. It eventually came through with Sikandar Raza leading the fight and staying there till the end.

50 runs in the last 5 overs have allowed Zimbabwe to finish strongly. A total of 277 is certainly competitive, but will it be match-winning? That remains to be seen. One thing is certain though, given the way they started, the hosts will feel they left a few runs out there. After Charith Asalanka got the call right at the toss, Sri Lanka’s new-ball attack failed to justify the decision to bowl first. They were wayward early on, and Ben Curran was quick to punish the loose deliveries.
Just a run to end the over. Dishes out a yorker-length delivery on off, Richard Ngarava plays it to cover for a single. Zimbabwe end with 277/7 on the board.

PITCH REPORT - Sikandar Bakht is near the deck. Informs that it is not the same surface as the last game. Feels that the characteristics will not be drastically different. Tino Mawoyo joins him and says that this track looks very similar to the previous game's surface. Points out a few cracks and reckons that those could result in uneven bounce. Believes that the covering of grass will hold the wicket together. Opines that Zimbabwe need to get to 300 to be competitive.

Sri Lanka's Janith Liyanage is also up for an interview. He admits that there was a bit of collapse, but points out that his partnership with Kamindu Mendis helped him play his natural game. He says that he tries to keep his composure and stay focused while batting. Admits that he will be honoured to become the fastest Sri Lankan batter to reach 1000 runs. Shares that he looks forward to playing more cricket outside the subcontinent and contributing to the team's performance.

Zimbabwe's Ben Curran is in for a chat. Shares that it was frustrating not to get over the line, but they have taken positives as a group. Feels that they did a lot of things right and will take those learnings into this game. States that losing two wickets in the first over is not ideal, so he and Sean Williams had to step back and soak in the pressure. Adds that he is happy with the way he played that situation.

The captain of Zimbabwe, Sean Williams says that he would have bowled first as well. Mentions that the previous game showed that you can get a good total here and they have the firepower to do so. Believes that there were plenty of positives and the guys are raring to go. Feels that they need to do the basics better than Sri Lanka and be proactive. Informs that they have made two changes with Ernest Masuku and Clive Madande coming into the side.

The Sri Lankan captain, Charith Asalanka calls it right at the toss and decides to bowl. He says that the wicket seemed to get better in the second innings in the last game and they want to take advantage of that. He also points out the brilliance of the team in the previous game and the way they managed to deliver under pressure. Shares that he looks forward to improving his performance as a batter and focuses on the positives from their last game. Adds that they hope to carry forward the momentum into this game. Informs that Nuwanidu Fernando comes in the playing XI.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favour of Charith Asalanka and Sri Lanka will BOWL first.

For Sri Lanka, Dilshan Madushanka’s hat-trick was, of course, the highlight, but there were strong contributions across the board. After a watchful start, the middle overs saw a wobble, but Janith Liyanage and Kamindu Mendis counterattacked brilliantly to post a total that had seemed far-fetched at one point. With the ball, Asitha Fernando impressed both upfront and at the death, partnering with Madushanka to seal the deal. Let's hope we are treated to another entertaining contest. Stay tuned for the toss and team news.

Despite the defeat, there were plenty of positives for Zimbabwe. Blessing Muzarabani and Richard Ngarava were excellent in setting the tone upfront with the new ball, and even after being 0/2 in the first over of the chase, they fought hard and came incredibly close to pulling off a win through Sikandar Raza's heroics. Sean Williams will continue to lead the side in the absence of Craig Ervine, who is sidelined with a calf strain. There is also uncertainty over Brendan Taylor’s participation after he suffered a dislocated finger in the first game, although he did manage to come out and bat.
